children: Infineon Technologies raised its artificial-intelligence sales forecasts for the new fiscal year, a sign it expects semiconductor demand to remain strong and the buildout of data centers to continue at pace.

The German chip maker said revenue from data centers in the year through September 2027 should be close to 4 billion euros, equivalent to $4.49 billion, up from prior guidance of roughly 2.5 billion euros.

The upgrade shows that Infineon expects AI demand to remain strong in the coming months despite fears from some investors that Democrats' win of majorities in both chambers of Congress could jeopardize the buildout of data centers.

Infineon, like other rivals that make chips needed to power data centers, has emerged as a beneficiary of hundreds of billions of dollars in spending commitments from some of the world's largest tech groups to build out AI infrastructure. Its stock is up more than 45% over the past 12 months.

AI is proving to be a valuable revenue stream for Infineon, making it less reliant on an auto industry that had been a source of pain for the company in recent years as carmakers slowly digested chip inventories they built at the height of the pandemic. That translated into subdued demand for Infineon's chips and several quarters of underwhelming sales. Now, even that end-market is recovering.

Chief Executive Jochen Hanebeck said he expected a significant increase in revenue and profitability in fiscal 2027, singling out semiconductors for data-center power supplies, the expansion and modernization of energy infrastructure, electromobility, and software-defined vehicles as key contributors.

For fiscal 2027, Infineon is projecting revenue of about 20 billion euros compared with 16.35 billion euros it reported for fiscal 2026. Its segment result margin is expected to come in the mid-twenties percentage range compared with 19.7% in fiscal 2026.

The timing of Infineon's fiscal year means the company is among the first chip makers in Europe to provide annual guidance, giving investors a sneak peek of where demand is heading. Its annual forecasts compare with analysts' estimate of 19.81 billion euros for revenue and a 24.9% margin, according to Vara Research.
Revenue for the three months to the end of September grew 19% from a year earlier to 4.71 billion euros, in line with analysts' forecasts, according to Vara Research.

Net profit climbed to 532 million euros from 231 million euros a year earlier. Its segment result--a key profitability measure--increased to 1.12 billion euros from 717 million euros, generating a 23.8% margin. Analysts had forecast a net profit of 678 million euros, a segment result of 1.10 billion euros and a 23.3% margin, according to Vara Research.
Infineon said it would propose a dividend of 0.38 euros a share for fiscal 2026 at its annual general meeting in February, above the  0.35 euros a share it paid for fiscal 2025.
